title: Homebrew download cache
what: Bottles, source archives and index files that Homebrew downloaded while installing or upgrading packages.
if_removed: Installed packages keep working, and Homebrew downloads files again only when you reinstall or upgrade.

title: npm cache
what: npm's cache of every package archive it has downloaded.
if_removed: The next install fetches packages from the registry again, so it is slower and needs a network connection.

title: pnpm store
what: The shared store that pnpm copies or links every project's packages from.
if_removed: Existing node_modules folders keep working, and the next install downloads packages into a fresh store.

title: Yarn classic cache
what: Yarn 1's offline copy of every package it has downloaded.
if_removed: The next yarn install downloads packages again from the registry.

title: Bun install cache
what: Packages that bun install has downloaded and keeps for reuse across projects.
if_removed: The next bun install downloads packages again.

title: pip cache
what: Python packages and built wheels that pip downloaded or compiled.
if_removed: pip downloads or rebuilds packages again the next time you install them.

title: uv cache
what: Python packages, wheels and source builds that uv keeps to make environments fast to create.
if_removed: Existing environments keep working, and uv downloads or rebuilds packages the next time it needs them.

title: Poetry cache
what: Package metadata and downloaded archives that Poetry caches, not including its virtual environments.
if_removed: Poetry downloads package information and archives again on the next install or lock.

title: Cargo registry cache and sources
what: Downloaded Rust crate archives and the unpacked source Cargo builds them from.
if_removed: Cargo downloads and unpacks crates again the next time a project builds.

title: Go build cache
what: Compiled packages and test results the Go toolchain reuses to make builds fast.
if_removed: The next go build or go test recompiles everything once, so it is slower that time.

title: Gradle caches
what: Dependencies, build outputs and transformed files that Gradle shares across projects.
if_removed: The next Gradle build downloads dependencies and rebuilds outputs again, which can take a while.

title: Cursor caches
what: Web, code and graphics caches the Cursor editor keeps to open windows and extensions faster.
if_removed: Cursor rebuilds them on its next launch, which may be slightly slower, and your settings and extensions are untouched.

title: VS Code caches
what: Web, code and graphics caches VS Code keeps to open windows and extensions faster.
if_removed: VS Code rebuilds them on its next launch, which may be slightly slower, and your settings and extensions are untouched.

title: Windsurf caches
what: Web, code and graphics caches the Windsurf editor keeps to open windows and extensions faster.
if_removed: Windsurf rebuilds them on its next launch, which may be slightly slower, and your settings and extensions are untouched.

title: Claude Code shell snapshots
what: Copies of your shell setup that Claude Code saves when a session starts so its commands run in a familiar environment.
if_removed: New sessions save a fresh snapshot, and snapshots older than a week belong to sessions that have ended.

title: Claude Code debug logs
what: Debug logs Claude Code writes for each session.
if_removed: You lose old debug output that is only useful when reporting a Claude Code bug.

title: Codex logs
what: Log files the Codex CLI and app write while they run.
if_removed: You lose old log output that is only useful when reporting a Codex bug.

title: App caches
what: Folders that apps keep in your ~/.cache folder, which the XDG standard reserves for data apps can recreate, untouched for a week.
if_removed: Apps may start a little slower the first time while they rebuild or re-download what they need, and no documents or settings are lost.

title: Go module cache
what: Source code of every Go module your projects have downloaded, the same folder go clean -modcache empties.
if_removed: Every Go project downloads its dependencies again on the next build, which needs a network connection and can take a while.

title: Project node_modules
what: Installed JavaScript packages inside a project you have not touched for 30 days and whose git state is committed and pushed.
if_removed: The project needs npm, pnpm, Yarn or Bun install before it runs or builds again.

title: Project Rust target
what: Rust build output inside a project you have not touched for 30 days and whose git state is committed and pushed.
if_removed: The next cargo build of that project compiles everything from scratch.

title: Project Python virtualenv
what: A Python virtual environment inside a project you have not touched for 30 days and whose git state is committed and pushed.
if_removed: The project needs its virtual environment recreated and packages reinstalled before it runs again.

title: Project Next.js build
what: Next.js build output and cache inside a project you have not touched for 30 days and whose git state is committed and pushed.
if_removed: The next dev server start or build of that project is slower while Next.js rebuilds it.

title: JetBrains IDE caches
what: Indexes, caches and the Local History of one JetBrains IDE version (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand and others), untouched for 30 days.
if_removed: The IDE re-indexes your projects the next time it opens them, and its Local History of past edits in that version is gone.

title: Maven local repository
what: Java libraries Maven and Gradle downloaded into the local repository, plus anything you installed there with mvn install.
if_removed: Builds download their dependencies again, and snapshot versions you only installed locally must be rebuilt from their source.

title: Flatpak app caches
what: Cache folders that Flatpak apps keep inside their own data folder under ~/.var/app.
if_removed: Each app rebuilds what it needs on its next start, and its documents and settings in the same folder are untouched.

title: Hugging Face hub cache
what: Model weights and datasets downloaded by Hugging Face libraries such as transformers and diffusers.
if_removed: Each model downloads again, often several gigabytes, the next time code loads it.

title: Codex worktrees
what: Separate git checkouts that Codex creates so tasks can run in parallel without touching your main checkout.
if_removed: Any uncommitted or unpushed work in that checkout leaves your disk with it, and git keeps listing the worktree until you run git worktree prune.

title: Old installers in Downloads
what: Installer packages and disk images (.deb, .rpm, .AppImage, .iso, .run) in your Downloads folder that are more than two weeks old.
if_removed: You would need to download an installer again to reinstall that app.

title: Downloaded AI models

owner.name: PyTorch, Whisper, llama.cpp and LM Studio

what: Model weights that PyTorch hub, OpenAI Whisper, llama.cpp and LM Studio downloaded into ~/.cache, often several gigabytes each.
if_removed: Each model downloads again, often several gigabytes, the next time a program loads it.

title: Ollama models
what: Local language models that Ollama downloaded, often several gigabytes each.
if_removed: Ollama has to download a model again before you can run it, so remove models with Ollama itself.

title: Claude Code session history
what: Transcripts of your Claude Code conversations, grouped by project, which also hold the context for resuming a session.
if_removed: You can no longer resume or search those conversations, so let Claude Code expire them itself.

title: Codex session history
owner_command: archive or delete old sessions from within Codex
what: Recorded Codex sessions, which Codex uses to resume and review past work.
if_removed: You can no longer resume or review those sessions, so manage them from Codex itself.

title: Docker Desktop disk image
what: The single disk image file that holds all of Docker Desktop's images, containers and volumes.
if_removed: Every image, container and volume is lost at once, so reclaim space with Docker's own prune commands instead.

title: Rootless Docker data
what: The images, containers, volumes and build cache of rootless Docker.
if_removed: Images, containers and volumes would be lost or corrupted, so reclaim space with Docker's own prune commands instead.

title: Podman storage
what: The images, containers and volumes of rootless Podman.
if_removed: Images, containers and volumes would be lost or corrupted, so reclaim space with Podman's own prune command instead.

title: Flatpak user installation
what: Flatpak apps and runtimes installed for your user only.
if_removed: Installed apps would stop working, so remove apps and unused runtimes with Flatpak itself.

title: Snap data
what: The per-user data folders of snap packages, one per app and revision.
if_removed: Snap apps would lose their settings and files, so remove snaps and their old revisions with snap itself.
